description.value: The study investigated insight deficits across frontotemporal dementia and Alzheimer's disease patients and examined their grey matter correlates using voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: The current study investigated insight deficit profiles across a large cohort of neurodegenerative patients (n = 81), including FTD and Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients.

value: Our predictions were that, similar to previous studies, FTD patients would show different profiles of insight deficits across domains, with bvFTD showing the most severe deficits.
Finally, we hypothesized that ventromedial prefrontal cortex atrophy would correlate with insight deficits, mirroring functional neuroimaging studies in the healthy.

value: Social interaction insight covaried with left orbitofrontal cortex, left parahippocampus, right middle temporal gyrus, bilateral insula, and right amygdala atrophy.
The social interaction condition was related to the lateral temporal lobe, which is similar to the FDG-PET findings reported by Ruby et al. (2007).

recruitment_method.value: Patients were sourced from the FRONTIER Dementia Clinic database in Sydney, Australia.

diagnostic_system.value: Current consensus FTD criteria (Neary et al., 1998; Rascovsky et al., 2011) for FTD diagnoses and NINCDS-ADRDA criteria for probable Alzheimer's disease.

spans.text: FTD patients met current consensus FTD criteria with insidious onset, decline in social behavior and personal conduct, emotional blunting and loss of insight (Neary et al.,1998; Rascovsky et al.,2011), while AD patients fulfilled NINCDS‐ADRDA criteria for probable AD (Tierney et al.,1988).

clinical_characteristics.value: The imaging subgroup comprised 13 bvFTD, 9 semantic dementia, 8 progressive non-fluent aphasia, 13 Alzheimer's disease, and 7 logopenic progressive aphasia patients. Disease severity was assessed with the Clinical Dementia Rating.
